content: 1. Meclizine and ziprasidone both enhance sedative effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Meclizine and zolpidem both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. Meclizine and zonisamide both elevate sedative effects. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Meclizine reduces zotepine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Monitor closely. 5. Meclizine decreases zotepine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 6. The combination of meclizine and zuranolone can lead to enhanced effects due to pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider reducing the dose. 7. Coadministration of zuranolone with other central nervous system (CNS) depressants may exacerbate psychomotor impairment or CNS depressant effects. If unavoidable, dose reduction should be considered. 8. Potential adverse effects of meclizine include drowsiness, thickening of bronchial secretions, acute glaucoma attacks, blurred vision (rare), constipation, fatigue, vomiting, xerostomia (dry mouth), headache, urinary retention, and hypersensitivity reactions. 9. Use caution when prescribing meclizine to patients with obstructive genitourinary tract disease, asthma, pyloric or duodenal obstruction, prostatic hyperplasia, or narrow-angle glaucoma. 10. Hepatic impairment may increase systemic exposure to meclizine. Renal impairment may lead to accumulation of meclizine or its metabolites. 11. Meclizine may impair physical or mental abilities. Patients should exercise caution when operating heavy machinery or performing tasks requiring mental alertness. 12. Meclizine is classified as Pregnancy Category B. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 13. It is not known whether meclizine is excreted in human milk; therefore, caution should be exercised when administering to lactating women. 14. Meclizine is an antihistamine with activity against nebulized histamine. It blocks the vasodepressor response to histamine and has slight blocking action against acetylcholine. 15. The onset of action for meclizine is 30–60 minutes, with a duration of 12–24 hours. Peak plasma levels are reached in approximately 3 hours. The volume of distribution (Vd) is 7 L/kg. 16. In vitro studies have identified CYP2D6 as the dominant metabolic enzyme for meclizine. 17. The half-life of meclizine is approximately 5 hours, and it is excreted via urine and feces. 18. Genetic polymorphism of CYP2D6, resulting in extensive, poor, intermediate, and ultrarapid metabolizer phenotypes, may contribute to significant interindividual variability in meclizine exposure. 19.
